sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the great shofar awakens the true will of every Jew to leave exile, distinguishing the future redemption from the Exodus.

translations.translation: And to add,
that according to what was said by my father-in-law, the Rebbe,
(in the maamar beginning "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown"54)
that the great shofar will awaken the point of Judaism within each and every Jew,
it is understood
that this—that all of Israel
(also including the lost and the banished)
will want to go out from exile and go to Jerusalem and bow down to Hashem—is that through the revelation of the great shofar, the true will55
of Israel will be awakened.
For this is the difference between the redemption from Egypt and the future redemption,
that in the Exodus from Egypt,
the desire of Israel to go out from the impurity of Egypt and to cleave to Him, blessed be He,56
was from the side of the revelation from Above,57
"He drew me,"58
but in the future redemption,
the will to go out from exile and come to Jerusalem will be the will of Israel itself,
and the revelation from Above
(the great shofar)
is only a cause through which the will of Israel is revealed.
And their service will be from their own selves—the virtue of Rosh HaShanah,
the service of man.59
However, regarding the lost and the banished in their simple sense,
the virtue of the service of man is after the revelation of the great shofar, through which his true will is awakened,
but the drawing down of the revelation of the great shofar is from the side of Above.
And there is another manner in "a great shofar shall be blown,"
that even the drawing down of the revelation of the great shofar is through service,
as above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section teaches that at the end of exile, service must be done with self-nullification, recognizing that all accomplishments come from Above, which strengthens rather than weakens one's work.

translations.translation: And this is "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown,"
that the instruction from this—that on that day a great shofar shall be blown,
it shall blow of itself—
is,
that at the end of the time of exile, when only a few moments remain before that day when the great shofar shall be blown
[and moreover, regarding several matters, the concept of "a great shofar shall be blown" has already begun,
as understood from the aforementioned maamar of my father-in-law, the Rebbe,60
and especially since from the time of the writing of the maamar until now many years have already passed,

and all the more so in recent times, when it has been seen tangibly that many who were initially in a state of lost and banished, heaven forfend, were awakened in teshuvah through the blowing of the great shofar61]
the service must be with self-nullification,
the recognition and feeling that all matters that were effected through one's service,
both regarding oneself and regarding others,
are not from the side of one's own virtues but from the side of the empowerment from Above.
And to note,
that this feeling does not cause weakness in one's service,
and on the contrary,
through this feeling,
one's service is with greater strength.
For when one's service is connected with his own existence,
the service is within measure and limitation.
And even when one's service is in the manner of "with all your might,"
it is still from "your might,"
from your own might,62
and through the feeling that the matters done through one's service are not from the powers he possesses but from the G-dliness,
through this he goes out from his own existence and limitations,
and his service is beyond measure and limitation.63

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that the great shofar must bring all Jews, including the lost and banished, to physically bow in Jerusalem through Moshiach speedily.

translations.translation: And behold, it is explained in the maamar beginning "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown"64
regarding the matter of the shofar of Rosh HaShanah,
that although the main drawing down is through the cry of the innermost heart, nevertheless the blowing must specifically be with a physical shofar,
because Asiyah is supernal,
and also in order that the revelation of the innermost supernal will
[the aspect of the supernal shofar65]
be drawn down below into physicality.
And from this it is understood,
that likewise regarding the blowing of the great shofar on that day,
the matters that were until now are not sufficient,
and the blowing of the great shofar must be in a manner that all of Israel,
also including the lost and the banished,
will come and bow down to Hashem on the holy mount in Jerusalem,
in physical Jerusalem,
through Moshiach our righteousness who will lead us upright to our land,
speedily in our days, very soon.
